text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, even for someone who did not write it. One key habit is following naming conventions: use clear, meaningful names for variables and functions so others can guess what they do. Another important idea is keeping functions small and focused on one task. This makes the code simpler to test and reuse. Clean code is also easier to maintain. When you need to fix a bug or add a feature later, well-organized code saves you time and reduces mistakes. In short, writing clean code helps both you and your team work more efficiently.
